reason: H0 only mutates archive bytes and drives the archive-read protocol through archive_read_open_memory, archive_read_next_header, archive_read_data_block, and the compatibility entry point archive_read_finish. It never exercises the newly public archive_write_free entry point or writer lifecycle states. This is material because archive_write_free may implicitly call archive_write_close and return an error, while shar_write immediately calls archive_error_string(a) after a failing archive_write_free(a), even though _archive_write_free frees a before returning. Thus the changed writer cleanup/error path contains a fuzz-worthy lifetime boundary absent from H0.
evidence: archive.h declares archive_write_free and states that it can fail when it implicitly calls archive_write_close.
_archive_write_free calls archive_write_close when the state is not ARCHIVE_STATE_CLOSED, then clears magic and executes free(a) before returning r.
shar_write evaluates archive_write_free(a) and, on failure, passes the freed a to archive_error_string(a).
H0 creates only archive_read_new objects and terminates them with archive_read_finish; it never calls archive_write_new, archive_write_free, or shar_write.

archive_read_finish is a compatibility wrapper that dispatches to the same archive_free vtable member, so H0 provides some indirect read-free implementation coverage but no corresponding writer-free coverage.
recommended_action: Add a stateful writer-lifecycle fuzz harness that drives archive_write_new through varied format/compression, open, header/data, explicit-close, implicit-close, and failing-close sequences, then calls archive_write_free and checks callers never inspect the freed archive object. Include direct coverage of shar_write's archive_write_free failure branch and analogous archive_write_disk cleanup states.
